rows.title: Scope
rows.pointer: MduX is not a medical device and performs no risk management process of its own against a device's intended use — it has none to evaluate against.

rows.title: Normative references
rows.pointer: Read alongside docs/iec62304/ and docs/iso13485/, which cover the two standards this one is written to work with.

rows.title: Terms and definitions
rows.pointer: [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-trust-zones-in-cpp.md)'s trust-zone architecture and [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-error-handling-and-exceptions-policy.md)'s exception-disabled governed zone are MduX's two concrete instances.

rows.title: Risk management process
rows.pointer: Device-level: MduX runs no risk management process of its own, and has no device whose life cycle one would span.

rows.title: Management responsibilities
rows.pointer: Device-level responsibility (providing resources, defining a risk acceptability policy, reviewing the process's suitability) belongs to a manufacturer's management, not to MduX.

rows.title: Competence of personnel
rows.pointer: MduX cannot attest to the competence of the people who developed it in the sense this clause asks a manufacturer to establish for its own risk management personnel.

rows.title: Risk management plan
rows.pointer: MduX has no device to plan risk management for.

rows.title: Risk management file
rows.pointer: MduX does not maintain one, because it is not the device.

rows.title: Risk analysis process
rows.pointer: Device-level; no MduX mechanism.

rows.title: Intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse
rows.pointer: MduX has no device-level intended use to state — a manufacturer's intended use for their device is what this sub-clause asks about, and MduX's role within that use is theirs to characterize, not this library's.

rows.title: Identification of characteristics related to safety
rows.pointer: The one MduX-level analog worth naming: which components of a *build* could affect safety if misconfigured — for instance, whether governed code can reach Vulkan or a windowing library.

rows.title: Identification of hazards and hazardous situations
rows.pointer: ADR-004 identifies a specific hazardous-situation category - a governed, safety-relevant module reaching Vulkan or a windowing library it should never touch - as one MduX's own architecture can foreclose regardless of the integrating device's specific use, rather than leaving every device manufacturer to rediscover it independently.

rows.title: Estimation of the risk(s) for each hazardous situation
rows.pointer: Estimating probability and severity requires a device-level context (who is exposed, what happens if the hazard occurs in *this* device) that MduX does not have.

rows.title: Risk evaluation
rows.pointer: Device-level: acceptability criteria belong to the manufacturer's risk management plan, and MduX has no standing to set them.

rows.title: Risk reduction, risk control option analysis
rows.pointer: MduX's own practice already follows that preference structurally, even though the analysis behind it happened at the architecture level rather than against a named device risk: [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-trust-zones-in-cpp.md)'s trust zones and [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-error-handling-and-exceptions-policy.md)'s exception policy are both inherent-safety-by-design measures — a `FATAL_ERROR` at configure time or a compile failure, not a runtime check or a warning label.

rows.title: Implementation of risk control measures
rows.pointer: mdux_verify_trust_zones() is a risk control measure implemented as a mechanical build-time check rather than a documented procedure: it walks a governed target's transitive link graph and fails the configure step if it reaches Vulkan or a windowing library, which is the hazardous-situation category identified in docs/iso14971/03-risk-analysis.md.

rows.title: Residual risk evaluation
rows.pointer: Because MduX's trust-zone check is a hard build failure rather than a probabilistic mitigation, residual risk for the category it covers is effectively zero - contingent on the check still running in CI.

rows.title: Risk/benefit analysis
rows.pointer: Device-level; MduX has no benefit analysis of its own to weigh against, since it is not the device delivering a clinical benefit.

rows.title: Risks arising from risk control measures
rows.pointer: MduX's trust-zone check fails the build rather than passing silently, so a misconfiguration of the control is visible immediately instead of leaving an undetected gap.

rows.title: Completeness of risk control
rows.pointer: Device-level: completeness is judged across a device's whole hazard list, which MduX cannot see from inside one dependency.

rows.title: Evaluation of overall residual risk
rows.pointer: Nothing in this corpus should be read as a claim that MduX's two identified hazard categories represent the totality of risk a device integrating MduX carries — they are the two categories MduX's own architecture happens to address, not an exhaustive analysis.

rows.title: Risk management review
rows.pointer: Device-level: a review before release is a management activity MduX has no release and no management to run.

rows.title: General
rows.pointer: Device-level, and dependent on there being a released device generating field information — MduX has neither yet.

rows.title: Collection of information
rows.pointer: MduX's nearest analog is far narrower: its own CI results and issue tracker are production information about *this repository*, not about a released device.

rows.title: Review of information
rows.pointer: Device-level; no MduX mechanism.

rows.title: Actions
rows.pointer: Device-level; no MduX mechanism, and no field to act on.
